slice: P6-D LAYER group-390 PlotStyleName mapping and loss refusal

autodeskLayerSchema.finding: LAYER group 390 is the hard-pointer ID/handle of a PlotStyleName object.

autodeskObjectARX.finding: AutoCAD resolves a layer plot-style name through the plot-style name dictionary and stores the resulting object reference in group 390.

implementation.change: DRW_Layer now exposes a non-consuming group-390 handle validator parallel to its group-347 material helper. The writer preserves explicit null, uses the historical F placeholder for absent/default input, resolves other explicit pointers through the caller resolver, and refuses unresolved nondefault handles instead of discarding them. AC1014 and earlier also refuse a supplied nondefault pointer because group 390 is unavailable there. Generated tests check destination rollback on refusal, then install a resolver on the same codec and verify AC1015 same-writer retry and fresh DXF readback of the mapped target in ASCII and Binary; a separate vector checks explicit null readback.

focusedTest.coverage: Existing seven-revision ASCII/Binary allocation rollback/retry and pre-R2000 refusal controls pass. New generated cases refuse AC1014 group-390 handle 0x123 without replacing a destination sentinel, retry at AC1015 using a resolver mapping 0x123 to 0x456, then read back group 390 as 456 in ASCII and Binary. The AC1027 case also checks unresolved-refusal, destination rollback, same-writer resolver retry, mapped-handle readback, and explicit-null preservation.

limits: The generated resolver callback is trusted to map into an emitted object graph; this test proves handle mapping and DXF readback, not target-object existence or ownership closure.
No native AutoCAD, BricsCAD, LibreCAD, or LibreCAD_3 plot-style semantic qualification was run.
Default absent-input F behavior is retained for compatibility and is not newly qualified against an independent consumer.
